messages:
michael_acme: We're seeing a sudden auth 401s and massive billing token spikes for EU customers starting ~10:12 UTC. All endpoints resolving to us-east for a subset of mobile ISPs. Anyone else?

alice_support: sorry about that — can you paste an example request id & timestamp?

michael_acme: req=01FZ9XQK, ts=2026-03-17T10:12:04Z. Quick sniff shows DNS answers flipped between eu-west and us-east quickly. Mobile carrier caches TTL weirdly. Repro steps below.

ben_netops: looks like an ISP transparent proxy returning stale A records. Can you run:
```
dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example.com
dig @1.1.1.1 +trace api.redwood.example.com
``` 
and paste outputs? Also are you seeing mixed geo headers (X-Redwood-Region)?

michael_acme: pasted outputs in DM. yes, sometimes header is `x-rw-region: eu-west`, sometimes `us-east`. Tokens issued by eu-west service expire when validated in us-east => 401.

carla_sre: that token mismatch explanation fits. Suspect TTL oscillation + ISP caching. Two quick mitigations: 1) Pin cert validation by region (short-term) 2) Force sticky routing for that customer (can route by IP prefix). I'll open a canary rule.

alice_support: filing escalation to routing + billing: customer seeing doubled token consumption billed in both regions when replays occur. @ben_netops any known prefilling/anycast issues this morning?

ben_netops: we had a GeoIP DB sync fail 10:05-10:11 UTC causing some POPs to de-prioritize eu-west, plus a CDN prefill that set a low TTL on some A records. ISP proxies apparently keep old copies and flip. Investigating source of TTL flip.

devops-bot: deploy finished: geoip-db v2026-03-17a rolled back at 10:15 UTC for rollback test. (deployment id: deploy-5492) :gear:

eng_oncall: immediate actions:
- Add customer IPs to sticky-route list (done 10:22 UTC)
- Create billing credit ticket for duplicate token charges
- Add temporary `x-rw-region-accept` header to allow cross-region token validation for 5m window

michael_acme: thanks — after sticky route appl, error rate dropped from 18% -> 0.7% for our sample. Billing spike still visible though, can confirm after credits.

carla_sre: next steps — we should publish a short KB for customers on mobile ISPs explaining transient TTL flips + recommended client-side backoff. Also add probe monitoring for DNS answer variance per ASN.

alice_support: i'll follow up with customer with the KB link + billing ticket id #3421. closing here once billing credits confirmed. :thumbsup:
